messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: paging @nate_oncall — high GPU pool queueing observed in us-east-1 (gpu-pool-alpha). Autoscaler hit max_instances, queue growth x3 in 6m. Suspected cause: rollout v27.4 of tokenizer service changed kv key hashing -> kv-cache fanout. Dash: https://redwood.dash/incident/4765432100

nate_oncall: On it. Looking at autoscaler logs and pool metrics. Do we have a rollout id?

mattl: That was the tokenizer v27.4 rollout - rolled at 15:02 UTC, canary succeeded then promoted. We started seeing queue rise ~15:08.

ana: (typo) ana_r: Confirming - new tokenizer changed prefix hashing: a lot of previously-shared KV prefixes are now unique, so warm cache hitrate dropped and every request is cold-priming kv-cache, increasing per-request GPU work.

elaine_sre: Key metrics: queue_length gpu-pool-alpha went from 120 -> 380; active_nodes 48 -> 48 (max cap 48). p95 latency increased from 120ms -> 2.3s. Error 502s from the inference proxy 0.6% -> 2.4%.

nate_oncall: Can we temporarily increase max_instances? If autoscaler upper bound is the blocker, bumping should buy time while we rollback.

mattl: I can patch autoscaler config but need approval — this is a reserved capacity limit for cost control. How many extra nodes needed?

elaine_sre: Estimate: to get queue under control we need ~20 extra GPUs for the short term. Current pool quota for us-east-1 is 80 but autoscaler config caps this pool at 48.

ana: Also feasible: divert some traffic to eu-west until cache warms and we complete either rollback or a tokenizer patch that restores previous hashing.

mattl: I'm starting an emergency rollback of tokenizer v27.4 to v27.3 on staging and will push to prod canary if safe. DeployBot, initiate rollback on prod canary.

deploy-bot: @mattl acknowledged. Starting rollback: rollout_id=rl_2026_27_4 -> rl_2026_27_3. Canary rollback started at 15:28 UTC. See: https://deploys/redwood/rl_2026_27_4/ops

nate_oncall: While rollback runs, please increase autoscaler cap to 70 for gpu-pool-alpha. @finance FYI — short-term cost spike.

mattl: Patching autoscaler config now. Command: ```
kubectl -n infra exec autoscaler-ctrl -- /bin/sh -c "apply-config --pool gpu-pool-alpha --max-instances 70"
```

elaine_sre: Patch applied. Autoscaler reported new max_instances=70. It will start provisioning; ETA ~2m for node spin-up given current spare capacity.

nate_oncall: Running quick check on queue and new node join logs: ```
curl -s https://infra/api/pools/us-east-1 | jq '.pools[] | select(.name=="gpu-pool-alpha") | {queue: .queue_length, active: .active_nodes, max: .max_nodes}'
# => {"queue":380, "active":48, "max":70}
```

mattl: Canary rollback completed at 15:32 UTC on ~10% traffic. Observing canary proxies: kv cache hitrate improved from 8% -> 38% on canary. Rolling full rollback in 1m if stable.

ana: Important note for followup: upstream tokenizer change changed how token prefixes are salted before hashing; this made previously identical prefixes distinct. Fix options: revert (we're doing), or reintroduce compatibility layer in tokenizer for hash normalization.

jamie-cs: Customer impact check: Two enterprise customers (org-id: E-781, E-332) reported slow responses and timeouts in the window 15:10–15:35 UTC. CS pinged both, asked to expect follow-up. No large-scale outage reported externally.

nate_oncall: After autoscaler patch new nodes are joining. Queue decreasing: 380 -> 220 in 3m. p95 down to 600ms. Good signal.

deploy-bot: Full rollback complete at 15:36 UTC. Traffic shifted back to v27.3.

elaine_sre: Post-rollback metrics: queue 220 -> 80 over next 7m, active_nodes climbing to 62 and then stabilizing at 54. p99 at 480ms currently. Error rate back to baseline 0.3%.

mattl: Confirming rollback successful and autoscaler cap remains at 70 for now. I'll schedule a controlled decrease to previous cap after we confirm no regression for 1h.

nate_oncall: Handoff to @elaine_sre for post-incident monitoring and root-cause followup. I'll update incident channel and run a quick postmortem checklist.

elaine_sre: Taking handoff. Action items: (1) create incident ticket with timeline and customer impact; (2) add model onboarding checklist to require KV-hash compatibility test; (3) investigate telemetry to detect sudden kv-cache hitrate deltas during rollouts; (4) revert autoscaler cap after 60m if stable.

jamie-cs: I'll send a customer summary to E-781 and E-332 with an apology + mitigation steps and ETA for full RCA.

nate_oncall: Incident mitigated. Marking status: mitigated -> monitoring. Root cause: tokenizer v27.4 changed kv-prefix hashing causing dramatic cache miss amplification and increased GPU work per request -> pool exhausted against autoscaler cap. Followups required for deployment checks and autoscaler default caps. :white_check_mark: 

IncidentBot: Incident record created: INC-4765432100. Severity: Sev2. Status: monitoring. Links: timeline, graphs, playbook.

elaine_sre: I'll own the postmortem. Draft ETA 24h. Adding reviewers: infra, eng-runtime, devex, product.

mattl: Notes for postmortem: add a checklist item to run a synthetic warmup for kv-prefix distribution when tokenizers change. Also consider autoscaler soft-limits that auto-burst for emergency rollbacks.

nate_oncall: Thanks all. Closing on-call thread; please keep updates in the incident ticket. :thanks:
